versions.text: Standard: An air system-level assessment, with integration of hardware and software, confirms that the fault accommodation features of the system provide a reaction, means for return to intended function, and vehicle recovery following a single failure or combination of failures more likely than an unacceptable rate as determined for the air system or program (e.g., improbable or lower quantitative probabilities in MIL-STD-882, Quantitative Probability Example). Means for return to intended function and vehicle recovery may include crewmember actions with WCAs and procedures. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination. (1) The system safety planning documentation includes the air system or program definition of the unacceptable rate for the air system or program (e.g., improbable or lower quantitative probabilities in MIL-STD-882, Quantitative Probability Example). (2) The FMET plan addresses verification of SCFs in addition to assessment of loss, degraded, and erroneous operation. The FMET addresses intended functionality of mitigations such as redundancy, monitoring, WCAs, and diagnostics. The FMET plan identifies, with rationale, the levels of the design intended for testing. (3) Review of hazard analyses for failure conditions with a catastrophic and critical severity, including review of FTAs, confirms no single failures or combination of failures more likely than the unacceptable rate. Analysis and frequency determination addresses the intended operational usage. Review design changes and mitigations, including mitigations in test planning documentation, that reduce the severity or frequency of any failure conditions to meet this standard. (4) Hazard tracking system review confirms verification of mitigation effectiveness to support execution to intended operational usage and positioning to begin flight test. Analysis. (1) Conduct failure mode and hazard analyses for the air system to determine the probability of failure occurrence. Analysis methodologies include the FMEA, FMECA, SSHA, SSA, and FTA; analyses may be documented in a comprehensive Safety Assessment Report. (2) The FMEA, FMECA, and other analyses address loss, degradation, and erroneous operation of SCFs and are inputs to FMET test plans and procedures. (3) Unsatisfactory results and unintended behavior observed during FMET, captured in problem or deficiency reports, undergo analysis and evaluation to identify corrective actions. Corrective actions may include mitigation measures, substantiated by the analysis, to support entry into flight test. (4) Conduct analysis of FMET results to assess the integration of hardware and software for verification of SCFs as well as the ability to react, means for return to intended function, and recover from a single failure or combination of failures. Means for return to intended function and vehicle recovery may include crewmember actions with WCAs and procedures. Test. (1) Lab test: The FMET comprehensively tests SCFs by injecting failure conditions into the system at appropriate levels of the design to confirm the ability to react, means for return to intended function, and recover from a single failure or combination of failures. Means for return to intended function and vehicle recovery may include crewmember actions with WCAs and procedures. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination. (5) Review of hazard analyses for failure conditions, updated based on flight test results, with a catastrophic and critical severity, including review of FTAs, confirms no single failures or combination of failures more likely than the unacceptable rate. Review design changes and mitigations, with evidence in requirements documentation and USG verified technical data, that reduce the severity or frequency of any failure conditions to meet this standard. (6) Hazard tracking system review confirms completion of mitigation effectiveness verification with evidence in requirements documentation and USG verified technical data. Analysis. (5) Conduct analysis of test results to assess the integration of hardware and software for verification of SCFs as well as the ability to react, means for return to intended function, and recover from a single failure or combination of failures. Means for return to intended function and vehicle recovery may include crewmember actions with WCAs and procedures. (6) Unsatisfactory results and unintended behavior observed during testing, captured in problem or deficiency reports, undergo analysis and evaluation to identify corrective actions. Evidence of corrective action implementation shows completion of changes to design, specification requirements, verification activities, and mitigations documented in USG verified technical data. (7) A SCF V&V coverage analysis confirms that the collective set of data provides for end-to-end verification for the function thread under nominal and off-nominal conditions for the intended air system operational usage. Analysis identifies gaps in V&V activities (e.g., incomplete end-to-end test coverage, failures in testing) and verifies adequacy of mitigations to ensure integrity of SCF operation. Test. (2) Flight or Ground test: For safety-critical functionality that was not evaluated during lab testing, conduct test to collect verification data on safety-critical functionality and effectiveness of mitigations, to include redundancy, monitoring, diagnostics, and notification to crewmembers. Problem or deficiency reports capture any unintended behaviors observed during verification and identify mitigations to address these behaviors. (3) Flight, Ground, or Lab test: Conduct regression testing to verify completion of mitigations or configuration changes implemented to address deficiency and problem reports identified in FMET and other test activities.
